mainTopic: Measuring a כזית for אבר מן החי and other forbidden foods: throat or stomach. The close of גיד הנשה and the opening משנה of כל הבשר
overview: The amud first finishes a point from the previous page: the איסור of טריפה can take effect on חלב, which has a permitted form, but not on an אבר מן החי, which never does. Next comes a case of a כזית-sized אבר מן החי split in two and eaten. רב דימי and רבין report differently what רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said. Everyone agrees that splitting it outside the mouth makes him פטור. When it is split inside the mouth, רבי יוחנן says חייב because his throat enjoyed a כזית, and in רבין's version ריש לקיש says פטור because a full כזית must reach the stomach. רבי אלעזר adds that he is חייב even if the limb was split outside the mouth. The same throat-versus-stomach argument explains their מחלוקת about food on the palate, as רב פפא clarifies. רבי יוחנן also rules that someone who ate half a זית, vomited it, and ate another half is liable. The story of רבי אלעזר reminding רבי אסי shows that the same idea applies when someone eats the same vomited half again. The פרק of גיד הנשה then ends, and פרק כל הבשר opens with a משנה forbidding all meat with milk, except fish and grasshoppers.

steps.title: A limb with no permitted form does not get the טריפה prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its distinction. חלב has a permitted form (the חלב of a חיה), so the טריפה איסור can take effect on it. An אבר מן החי has no permitted form, so the טריפה איסור does not take effect on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...to its general prohibition. But a limb, which has no permitted form at all, does not get the prohibition of טריפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began before this section. It closes the distinction between חלב and אבר מן החי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור that is כולל can only take effect on something that is not already totally forbidden in every form. חלב is permitted in some cases (from a חיה), so a second איסור can still take hold. An אבר מן החי is never permitted, so the טריפה איסור cannot be added on top of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Has a permitted form somewhere within its general category
A limb taken from a living animal
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: A new איסור can take effect on חלב because חלב is sometimes permitted. It cannot take effect on an אבר מן החי, which is never permitted.

phrases.english: ...from its general category; but a limb,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from before: חלב is 'permitted from its general category,' because the חלב of a חיה is allowed.

phrases.english: which was not permitted from its general category, no.
phrases.notes: 'No' means the טריפה prohibition does not take effect on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל אבר דלא הותר מכללו לא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the argument from the previous part of the דף
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The איסור of טריפה does not take effect on an אבר מן החי, because an אבר is never permitted.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about a limb split outside the mouth
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן what the law is if someone split a כזית-sized אבר מן החי in two outside his mouth and then ate the pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן, 'If he split it outside his mouth, what is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about eating אבר מן החי. It reports a question ריש לקיש asked his teacher רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a limb that is exactly a כזית. If it is cut in two before eating, each piece is less than a כזית, and neither piece is a whole limb anymore. The question is whether he is still punished.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came. Used for a sage who brought a teaching from ארץ ישראל to בבל
He split it, meaning he divided the limb into two pieces
Outside, meaning outside his mouth
What is it? (what is the law?)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish asked Rabbi Yochanan:
If he split it outside, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'It' is a limb from a living animal that is exactly a כזית, and 'outside' means outside his mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי אתא רב דימי אמר בעא מיניה רבי שמעון בן לקיש מרבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about eating אבר מן החי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is someone liable if he splits a כזית-sized limb outside his mouth and eats the two halves?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: split outside means פטור
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the first question. Someone who cut the limb before putting it in his mouth is not punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the limb is cut outside, he never eats a full כזית of a whole limb in one go. Each piece is too small, so there is no punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt, meaning not punished
The size of an olive, the minimum amount for punishment

phrases.english: He said to him: Exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה פטור
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Splitting the limb outside the mouth makes him פטור.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about a limb split inside the mouth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש follows up: what if he put the whole limb into his mouth and split it there?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he split it inside his mouth, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש asks a follow-up question. This time the limb is split only after the whole thing is already in his mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference from the first case is that the whole כזית limb was in his mouth at one time. The question is whether that counts as eating a whole limb, even though he swallowed it in two pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside, meaning inside his mouth
What? (what is the law?)

phrases.english: Inside, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: מבפנים מאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question built on the answer in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is someone liable if he splits the limb only after it is inside his mouth?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: split inside means חייב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that splitting the limb inside the mouth does not help. The person is punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, what matters is that the whole limb was in his mouth at once. Splitting it afterward does not remove the liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable, meaning punished
Lashes, the punishment for eating a forbidden food

steps.whatToRemember: In רב דימי's version, רבי יוחנן rules פטור when the limb is split outside the mouth and חייב when it is split inside, and ריש לקיש does not argue.

phrases.english: He said to him: Liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה חייב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the follow-up question in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Splitting the limb inside the mouth makes him חייב.

steps.title: רבין's version: split inside is a מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports the discussion differently. Everyone agrees that splitting outside makes him פטור, but for splitting inside, רבי יוחנן says חייב and ריש לקיש says פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: If he split it outside, he is exempt. If he split it inside, רבי יוחנן says he is liable, and ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of the same discussion from another traveler, רבין. In his version, the inside case is a disagreement and not a simple question and answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports agree on the outside case (פטור) and on רבי יוחנן's view of the inside case (חייב). The only difference is ריש לקיש. In רב דימי's version he just asked the question, but in רבין's version he holds that even splitting inside the mouth makes him פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: If split outside, he is exempt. Both versions agree on this point
Inside the mouth. This is the case where רבין's version has a disagreement

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same story told two ways, not two different cases. The only change is whether ריש לקיש disagrees about the inside case.
steps.whatToRemember: Splitting outside makes him פטור according to everyone. Splitting inside makes him חייב according to רבי יוחנן, and in רבין's version ריש לקיש says פטור.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
If he split it outside, he is exempt;
inside, Rabbi Yochanan says he is liable,
and Reish Lakish says he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי אתא רבין אמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different report of the same discussion found in steps 2 to 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Splitting outside makes him פטור according to everyone. Splitting inside is a מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן says חייב and ריש לקיש says פטור.

steps.title: The reasons behind each side's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he is liable because his throat enjoyed a full כזית. ריש לקיש says he is exempt because a full כזית has to reach the stomach together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is חייב, because his throat enjoyed a כזית. ריש לקיש says he is פטור, because we need the eating to count in the stomach, and that did not happen here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבין's version from Step 6 and explains why each side rules the way he does about a limb split inside the mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the eating is measured at the throat. The whole כזית was in his mouth together, so the throat enjoyed a full כזית. For ריש לקיש, the eating is measured in the stomach. Since the pieces went down one at a time, a full כזית never arrived there at once.

keyTerms.meaning: His throat enjoyed: the eating is measured by the pleasure of the throat
Eating measured in the stomach (literally, 'in his innards')
An olive-sized amount, the minimum amount of food that makes someone liable
We require it, and it isn't there

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic question about what 'eating' means in הלכה: is it the throat's enjoyment or the food arriving in the stomach? The rest of this section builds on that question.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he is liable,
phrases.notes: This is the case from Step 6, where he put the whole limb in his mouth and split it there.

phrases.english: for his throat has enjoyed an olive-bulk.
And Reish Lakish says: he is exempt,
we require eating in his stomach, and there is none.
phrases.notes: He means a whole כזית reaching the stomach at one time, which didn't happen because the pieces went down separately.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חַיָּיב, הֲרֵי נֶהֱנָה גְּרוֹנוֹ בִּכְזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the argument reported by רבין in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: liability is measured by the throat's enjoyment. ריש לקיש: liability needs a full כזית to reach the stomach at once.

steps.title: How could anyone ever be liable according to ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how, according to ריש לקיש, a person could ever be liable for eating a limb, since food normally gets broken up before it is swallowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי שמעון בן לקיש, how can you find a case where someone is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's view by asking whether it leaves any realistic case of liability. This sets up רב כהנא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People chew their food, so a limb almost always breaks apart in the mouth. If splitting in the mouth makes him exempt, the איסור of eating a limb from a living animal would seem almost impossible to violate.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find it? Asking for a case where the law could actually apply
Is liable

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
how can you find a case where he is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ דִּמְחַיֵּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's reasoning from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's position that splitting in the mouth makes him exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since food is normally broken up before swallowing, his view seems to leave no practical case of liability for אבר מן החי.

steps.title: רב כהנא: a small bone swallowed whole
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that he is liable when the limb is a tiny one, a small bone with meat, that can be swallowed whole as a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: it is talking about a small bone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends ריש לקיש by giving a case where he would be liable: a limb small enough to swallow whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny limb, with its bone, meat and sinew together, can be about a כזית and go down in one swallow. Then a full כזית reaches the stomach at once, so even ריש לקיש agrees he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A small bone, meaning a tiny limb with its meat that can be swallowed whole
A limb taken from a living animal, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: With a small bone.
phrases.notes: He means a tiny limb, with its meat on it, small enough to swallow in one go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: בִּגְרוֹמִיתָא זְעֵירְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש's view seems to leave no case of liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is liable when a small limb is swallowed whole, so a full כזית reaches the stomach at once.
steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, liability for eating a limb needs a full כזית reaching the stomach at once, such as a small limb swallowed whole.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: even splitting outside makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that even if he split the limb outside his mouth, he is still liable, because pieces that only need to be brought together are not 'missing an action.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: even if he split it outside his mouth, he is also liable. Being missing only 'bringing together' is not like being missing an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with the case that everyone in Step 6 agreed on, and says that splitting outside the mouth also makes him liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said splitting outside makes him exempt. רבי אלעזר says the two pieces still make up the whole limb; they are only missing being put back next to each other. That is not considered a real missing act, so he ate the full amount.

keyTerms.meaning: He split it outside his mouth
Missing only being brought close together
Missing a real action, something that still needs to be done
Is not similar to

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix him up with the earlier speakers. In Step 6 everyone agreed that splitting outside makes him פטור. רבי אלעזר is a new, separate opinion that says חייב even there.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
Even if he split it outside, he is also liable,

phrases.aramaic: מְחוּסַּר קְרִיבָה לָאו כִּמְחוּסַּר מַעֲשֶׂה דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: being lacking only bringing-close is not like lacking an action.
phrases.notes: The two pieces just need to be put back next to each other, and that doesn't count as anything missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חִלְּקוֹ מִבַּחוּץ נָמֵי חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the 'split outside' case from Steps 2-3 and 6 and gives a different ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a limb split outside the mouth makes him liable, because lacking only 'bringing together' is not lacking an action.

steps.title: Does food stuck between the teeth count toward the כזית?
steps.stepSummary: A new argument: ריש לקיש says the כזית does not include food stuck between the teeth, and רבי יוחנן says it does include that food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says: the כזית the חכמים spoke about does not include what stays between the teeth. רבי יוחנן says: it even includes what is between the teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new argument between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן about how to measure a כזית for eating prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches their earlier reasoning in Step 7. ריש לקיש measures by what reaches the stomach, so food stuck in the teeth doesn't count. רבי יוחנן measures by the throat and mouth enjoying it, so even food left between the teeth counts toward the כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: The olive-sized amount that the חכמים set for eating prohibitions
Between the teeth, food that gets stuck and isn't swallowed
Except for, not including
Even together with, including

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש consistently measures eating by what reaches the stomach, and רבי יוחנן by what the mouth and throat enjoy. This explains both their arguments here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּזַיִת שֶׁאָמְרוּ – חוּץ מִשֶּׁל בֵּין הַשִּׁינַּיִם,
phrases.english: The olive-bulk that they spoke of excludes what is between the teeth,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף עִם בֵּין הַשִּׁינַּיִם.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says: even including what is between the teeth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: כְּזַיִת שֶׁאָמְרוּ – חוּץ מִשֶּׁל בֵּין הַשִּׁינַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related argument between the same two אמוראים about measuring a כזית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: food stuck between the teeth does not count toward the כזית. רבי יוחנן: it does count.

steps.title: רב פפא narrows the argument to food on the palate
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says nobody counts food stuck between the teeth. The מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש is only about food left on the palate. רבי יוחנן says the throat enjoyed a כזית, and ריש לקיש says we need a כזית of eating in the stomach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: About food between the teeth, everyone agrees it does not count. Where they argue is about food on the palate. One master holds that his throat already enjoyed a כזית. The other master holds that we need the eating to be in his stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא reframes the argument from step 11. He says it is not really about food between the teeth. It is about food that stays on the palate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says both sides agree that food stuck between the teeth does not count. The argument is only about food left on the palate, which was tasted but not swallowed. רבי יוחנן, who follows the throat's enjoyment, counts it. ריש לקיש, who needs a full כזית to reach the stomach, does not count it.

keyTerms.meaning: On the palate or gums, meaning food that was tasted but not swallowed
Everyone agrees; there is no argument here
One master holds (used to set out each side of an argument)
His throat enjoyed it, meaning the pleasure of tasting and swallowing
Eating measured by what arrives in the stomach

steps.confusionAlert: Do not keep thinking the argument is about food between the teeth, as step 11 sounded. רב פפא says both sides agree that food doesn't count. The real argument is only about food on the palate.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
With regard to food between the teeth –
everyone agrees,
phrases.notes: He means everyone agrees it does NOT count toward the כזית.

phrases.english: where they argue – is about food on the palate.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: הֲרֵי נֶהֱנָה גְּרוֹנוֹ בִּכְזַיִת,
phrases.english: One master holds: his throat has enjoyed an olive-size,
phrases.notes: This first master is רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: we need the eating to be in his stomach.
phrases.notes: This second master is ריש לקיש.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֶׁל בֵּין שִׁינַּיִם דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Redefines the exact case of the argument quoted in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food between the teeth never counts. Food on the palate counts for רבי יוחנן, who follows the throat, but not for ריש לקיש, who follows the stomach.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: two half-olives with vomiting in between
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן. Someone ate half a זית of forbidden food, vomited it, and then ate another half. He is liable, because his throat enjoyed a full כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone ate half a זית and vomited it, and then ate another half זית, he is liable. Why? Because his throat enjoyed a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of רבי יוחנן that uses the same 'throat' reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full כזית was never in his stomach together, because the first half came back up. Still, רבי יוחנן says he is liable, since the throat swallowed a full כזית in total. This fits his view that liability follows the throat, not the stomach.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive-size, which is less than the amount needed for liability
He vomited it up
Liable, here meaning to receive lashes
What is the reason?

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the key source for step 17's challenge, because it shows that רבי יוחנן follows the throat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
If one ate half an olive-size and vomited it,

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר וְאָכַל חֲצִי זַיִת אַחֵר – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and then ate another half olive-size – he is liable.
What is the reason?
Because his throat has enjoyed an olive-size.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling that uses the same 'throat' reasoning as step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-olives eaten one after the other add up to liability even if the first was vomited, because the throat enjoyed a full כזית.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks about re-eating the vomited half-olive
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks רבי אסי about a case where someone ate half a זית, vomited it, and then ate that same half again. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked רבי אסי: If someone ate half a זית, vomited it, and then ate it again, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר raises a question about a new case. This sets up the גמרא's next move, which is figuring out what exactly he is asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference from step 13 is that the same half-זית is eaten twice, not a new half. The question is whether this adds up to a full כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, meaning he raised a question he was unsure about
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked Rabbi Asi:
If one ate half an olive-size and vomited it
and then ate it again, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מֵרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a variation of step 13's case, where the same half is eaten again.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether eating the same vomited half-זית a second time completes a כזית for liability.

steps.title: What is the question? Not about digestion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר is really unsure about. It cannot be whether vomited food counts as already digested, because then he should have asked about a full כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he asking? If he is asking whether the vomited food counts as digested or not, he should have asked about a whole כזית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pin down what רבי אלעזר's question is about. It tests one possible meaning and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One possibility is that he wants to know whether vomited food is considered 'digested,' which would make it no longer count as food. But that question would come up just as clearly with a full כזית. So mentioning a half-זית must mean the question is about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What exactly is he unsure about?
Digestion, meaning food that is already partly digested and no longer counts as food
Then let him ask about (a simpler case)

phrases.english: What is he asking?
If it is whether it counts as digested
or does not count as digested,
then let him ask about a whole olive-size!
phrases.notes: In other words, choosing a half-זית only makes sense if the question is about adding up halves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes and narrows the meaning of רבי אלעזר's question from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real point that רבי אלעזר is unsure about.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the question as being about digestion.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A question about digestion would be asked with a full כזית, not a half.

steps.title: The real question: throat or stomach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי אלעזר is asking whether we measure the כזית by the throat or by the stomach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is asking: do we go after his throat, or do we go after his stomach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer about what רבי אלעזר meant. He wants to know whether the throat or the stomach decides the measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The throat swallowed a total of a full כזית, half and then the same half again. But only half a זית ever ended up staying in the stomach. So the case tests which one counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the correct explanation after rejecting one)
We go after, meaning we decide based on

phrases.english: Rather, whether we go after his throat,
or whether we go after his stomach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי בָּתַר גְּרוֹנוֹ אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct meaning of the question after step 15 rejected the first possibility.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is whether liability is measured by the throat or by the stomach.

steps.title: Why not answer it from רבי אסי's report?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי אסי himself reported that רבי יוחנן follows the throat, so the question should already be answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him answer it from what רבי אסי said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. It asks why רבי אלעזר is unsure when רבי אסי already quoted a clear ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13, רבי אסי quoted רבי יוחנן making someone liable for two half-olives with vomiting in between, 'because his throat enjoyed a כזית.' That shows we follow the throat. So why would רבי אלעזר ask רבי אסי, of all people, about throat versus stomach?

keyTerms.meaning: Resolve it, meaning settle the question from a known source

phrases.english: Then let him resolve it from what Rabbi Asi said!
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אסי's report in step 13: 'his throat enjoyed a כזית.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מִדְּרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of the question given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that רבי אלעזר was unsure whether we follow the throat or the stomach.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אסי's own report of רבי יוחנן (step 13) already shows that we follow the throat, so there should be nothing left to ask.

steps.title: רבי אסי forgot, and רבי אלעזר came to remind him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר was not really unsure. רבי אסי had forgotten his learning, and רבי אלעזר's question was a reminder. He hinted that the case of re-eating the same half-זית teaches two rules: vomited food is not considered digested, and liability depends on the throat enjoying a full כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי forgot what he had learned, and רבי אלעזר came to remind him. This is what he was telling him: Why do you need a case of 'another' half-olive? Teach the case with the same half-olive! From that case we can learn two things. First, the food was not counted as digested. Second, he is liable because his throat enjoyed a full כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 17. רבי אלעזר's question was not a real question; he was reminding רבי אסי of something רבי אסי had forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was: why ask, if רבי אסי already reported that רבי יוחנן follows the throat? The answer is that רבי אסי had forgotten. רבי אלעזר was nudging him toward the better case, the same half-זית eaten twice, because that one case proves two rules at once.

keyTerms.meaning: His learning was uprooted from him, meaning he forgot what he had learned
To remind him
With the same one, the very same half-זית he vomited
Digestion; food that is considered already digested no longer counts as eating
His throat enjoyed it; the throat is where the pleasure of eating is measured

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי אלעזר's words in Step 14 as a real doubt. He knew the answer and was asking so that רבי אסי would remember it himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same-half-זית case shows that vomited food is not treated as digested. It also shows that the כזית is measured by the throat's enjoyment.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi had forgotten his learning,
and Rabbi Elazar came to remind him,
and this is what he was saying to him:
Why do I need another half-olive?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יוחנן's case in Step 13, where he ate a different, second half-זית.

phrases.english: Let the master say it with the same one,
since two things can be learned from it:
we learn from it that it does not count as digested,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמְעִינַן מִינַּהּ דַּהֲרֵי נֶהֱנָה גְּרוֹנוֹ בִּכְזַיִת.
phrases.english: and we learn from it that his throat has enjoyed a full olive-size.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי גְּמָרֵיהּ אִיעֲקַר לֵיהּ, וַאֲתָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְאַדְכּוֹרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 by explaining that the question was really a reminder.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the question: it was a reminder, not a real doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר did not know whether we measure by the throat or the stomach, even though רבי אסי had already reported רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אסי had forgotten, and רבי אלעזר was guiding him back to the same-half-זית case, which teaches two rules at once.

steps.title: רבי אסי is silent, and רבי אלעזר reminds him directly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי does not respond. רבי אלעזר then reminds him openly: 'Wonder of the generation, didn't you say this many times before רבי יוחנן, and he told you the reason is that his throat enjoyed a כזית?'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי was silent and said nothing at all. רבי אלעזר said to him: 'Wonder of the generation! Didn't you say this case many times in front of רבי יוחנן, and he told you: his throat has enjoyed a full כזית?'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. When the hint does not work, רבי אלעזר tells רבי אסי outright that he had heard this ruling from רבי יוחנן many times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the answer in Step 18 that רבי אסי had truly forgotten. רבי אלעזר respectfully calls him 'wonder of the generation' while reminding him. He shows that רבי יוחנן's reason, 'his throat enjoyed a כזית', applied to this very case.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent
Wonder of the generation; a title of great respect
Many times

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling is that eating is measured by the throat's enjoyment. So someone who eats the same half-זית twice, after vomiting it, is liable as if he ate a full כזית.

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי,
phrases.english: He was silent and did not say anything at all to him.
He said to him: Wonder of the generation,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר speaking to רבי אסי, giving him a warm, respectful title.

phrases.english: did you not say it many times
in front of Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לָךְ: הֲרֵי נֶהֱנָה גְּרוֹנוֹ בִּכְזַיִת?
phrases.english: and he told you: His throat has enjoyed a full olive-size?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of Step 18 and confirms that רבי אסי had forgotten.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי אסי had forgotten, and that רבי יוחנן's 'throat' reasoning covers the same-half-זית case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's report that רבי אסי said this case many times before רבי יוחנן and received this answer.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק גיד הנשה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing formula marks the end of the chapter of גיד הנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, גיד הנשה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the chapter. It is not part of the argument; it marks that the פרק of גיד הנשה is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional formula said when finishing a chapter. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again. The next line begins a brand-new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said at the end of a chapter
The sciatic nerve; the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, Gid HaNasheh.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter of גיד הנשה is complete.

steps.title: Opening משנה: all meat is forbidden with milk, except fish and grasshoppers
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens with a משנה. All meat may not be cooked in milk, and may not be placed on the table together with cheese. Fish and grasshoppers are the exception to both rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All meat is forbidden to cook in milk, except for fish and grasshoppers. And it is forbidden to bring meat up onto the table with cheese, except for fish and grasshoppers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה that sets out two rules about meat and milk. Fish and grasshoppers are excluded from both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule is about cooking meat in milk. The second rule goes further: meat and cheese may not even be placed on the same table. Fish and grasshoppers are not covered by either rule, so they may be cooked with milk and served with cheese.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
Meat with milk; the prohibition of mixing them
To bring up onto the table; to serve them together
Cheese
Fish and grasshoppers; excluded from the meat-and-milk rules

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the main chapter of שס on meat and milk. It also sets the basic scope of which kinds of 'meat' are included.

phrases.english: Mishnah: All meat
is forbidden to cook in milk,
except for the meat of fish and grasshoppers,
and it is forbidden to bring it up with cheese
onto the table,
except for the meat of fish and grasshoppers.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַבָּשָׂר אָסוּר לְבַשֵּׁל בְּחָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All meat is forbidden to cook in milk and to place on the table with cheese, except fish and grasshoppers.
